<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
Let $X_{\bullet}\colon (\mathbb{R},\leq)\to \mathrm{Top}$ be a persistent space. Then the \emph{persistent topological complexity} of $X_{\bullet}$ is the functor 
   $ \mathbf{TC}(X_{\bullet})\colon (\mathscr{Int},\subseteq)\to (\mathbb{N}\cup \{0\})$, defined by  \[\mathbf{TC}(X_{\bullet})([a,b])=\mathbf{TC}_G(f^b_a:X_a\to X_b).\] Here $\mathbf{TC}(f)$ denote the topological complexity of a map $f$ introduced in \cite{Sc}.
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- definition-2: body_md -->
Let $(\mathcal{P},\leq)$ denote the poset category. A \emph{persistent object} in a category $\mathcal{C}$ is a functor $X\colon \mathcal{P}\to \mathcal{C}$. 

    Thus for each object $a$ of $\mathcal{P}$, we have an object $X_a$ in $\mathcal{C}$ and for every object $a, b$ in $\mathcal{C}$ with $a\leq b$, there is a morphism $f^b_a\colon X_a\to X_b$ such that $f^a_a=\mathrm{id}_{X_a}$ and $f^a_c= f^b_c\circ f^a_b$ for every $a\leq b\leq c$.
<!-- end definition-2 -->
<!-- definition-3: body_md -->
The \emph{Lusternik--Schnirelmann category} of a persistent space $X_\bullet\in \mathrm{Top}^{(\mathbb{R},\leq)}$ is the functor
\(\mathbf{cat}(X_\bullet)\colon
(\mathscr{Int},\subseteq)\longrightarrow
(\mathbb{N}\cup\{\infty\},\leq)\), defined by  \[\mathbf{cat}(X_{\bullet})([s,t])= \mathbf{cat}_G(f^s_t\colon X_s\to X_t), 
\]
where $\mathbf{cat}(f)$ denotes the LS category of the map $f$ (see \cite{DK23}).
<!-- end definition-3 -->
<!-- definition-4: body_md -->
The \emph{persistent zero-divisor cup length} of a persistent space $X_{\bullet}\in \mathrm{Top}^{(\mathbb{R},\leq )}$ is the functor 
    \(\mathbf{zcl}(X_{\bullet}):(\mathscr{Int},\subseteq)\to (\mathbb{N}\cup \{\infty\})\),  defined by  \[\mathbf{zcl}(X_{\bullet})([a,b])=\mathbf{zcl}\big((f^b_a\times f^b_a)^{\ast}:\ker{(\Delta_{X_a})^{\ast}} \to \ker{(\Delta_{X_b})^{\ast}}\big).\]
<!-- end definition-4 -->
<!-- definition-5: body_md -->
\emph{Translation} on a preordered set $(P,\leq)$ is a functor $\Gamma\colon P\to P$ with a natural transformation $\eta_{P} \colon I_P\Rightarrow \Gamma$.
<!-- end definition-5 -->
<!-- definition-6: body_md -->
Let $G$ be a group and $\mathcal{C}$ be a category. We define $\mathcal{C}^G: = Func(BG,\mathcal{C})$, where $BG$ is the one-object category whose automorphism group is $G$.
    
    Then clearly the object of $\mathcal{C}^G$ is an object $X\in \mathcal{C}$ with a $G$-action $\rho\colon G\to \mathrm{Aut}(X)$ and morphisms are $G$-equivariant morphism.
<!-- end definition-6 -->
<!-- definition-7: body_md -->
A \emph{persistent $G$-object} in a category $\mathcal{C}$ is a functor $F\colon (P,\leq)\to \mathcal{C}^G$, where $(P,\leq)$ is preorderd set.
<!-- end definition-7 -->
<!-- definition-8: body_md -->
Let $P$ be a preordered set and let $\Gamma, K\in \textbf{Trans}_P$. Suppose $F,G\in \mathcal{C}^G$. Then a $G$-$(\Gamma,K)$-interleaving between $F$ and $G$ consists of natural transformations $\phi\colon F\Rightarrow G\Gamma$ and $\psi\colon G\Rightarrow FK$ such that $(\psi\Gamma)\phi= F\eta_{K\Gamma}$ and $(\phi K)\psi=G \eta_{\Gamma K}$.

    We say that $F, G$ are \emph{$G$-$(\Gamma,K)$-interleaved} if there exists a $G$-$(\Gamma,K)$-interleaving between them. 
    For brevity, a $G$-$(\Gamma,\Gamma)$-interleaving is simply termed $(\Gamma,G)$-interleaved.
<!-- end definition-8 -->
<!-- definition-9: body_md -->
We call a translation $\Gamma$ an \emph{$\epsilon$-translation} if $\omega_{\Gamma}\leq \epsilon$, where $\omega\colon \textbf{Trans}_P\to [0,\infty)$ is sublinear projection (see \cite{BDS}).

    $F,G \in \mathcal{C}^G$ are \emph{$G$-$\epsilon$-interleaved} with respect to $\omega$ if there exist $\epsilon$-translations $\Gamma, K\in \textbf{Trans}_P$ such that $F$ and $G$ are $G$-$(\Gamma,K)$-interleaved.
<!-- end definition-9 -->
<!-- definition-10: body_md -->
The \emph{$G$-interleaving distance} between $F, G\in \mathcal{C}^G$ is 
    \[d_{I}^{G\omega}(F,G):=\mathrm{inf}\{\epsilon\mid F,G \text{ are } G\text{-}\epsilon\text{-interleaved with respect to }\omega\}.\]
<!-- end definition-10 -->
<!-- definition-11: body_md -->
The $G$-Gromov-Hausdorff distance between $G$-metric spaces $(X,d_X^G)$ and $(Y,d_Y^G)$ is defined by $$d_{GH}^G(X,Y)=\frac{1}{2}\inf_{C\in \Gamma_G(X,Y)} \sup_{(x,y),(x',y')\in C} |d_X^G(x,x')-d_Y^G(y,y')|,$$
    where $\Gamma_G(X,Y)$ denotes the set of $G$-equivariant correspondence between $X$ and $Y$, that is, the set consisting all $G$-invariant subsets of $X\times Y$.
<!-- end definition-11 -->
<!-- definition-12: body_md -->
The equivariant topological complexity of a $G$-map $f\colon X\to Y$, denoted by $\mathbf{TC}_G(f)$, is the smallest non-negative integer $n$ for which there is a $G$-invariant open cover $\{U_0,\dots,U_n\}$ of $X\times X$, such that for each $i=0,\dots,n$, there is a $G$-map $s_i\colon U_i\to Y^I$ satisfying $s_i(x_0,x_1)(0)=f(x_0)$ and $s_i(x_0,x_1)(1)=f(x_1)$. If no such $n$ exists, we define $\mathbf{TC}_G(f)=\infty$.
<!-- end definition-12 -->
<!-- definition-13: body_md -->
Let $f\colon X \to Y$ be a $G$-map.  
The \emph{equivariant LS category} of $f$, denoted $\mathbf{cat}_G(f)$, is the least integer $n\geq 0$ such that $X$ admits a cover $\{U_i\}_{i=0}^n$ by $n+1$ $G$-invariant open subsets with the property that, for each $i$, the restriction $f|_{U_i}$ is $G$-homotopic to a $G$-map $U_i\to Y$ whose image lies in the orbit of some $y_i\in Y$.  
If no such $n$ exists, we set $\mathbf{cat}_G(f)=\infty$.
<!-- end definition-13 -->
<!-- definition-14: body_md -->
The $G$-equivariant zero divisor cup length of a $G$-map $f\colon X\to Y$, denoted by $\mathbf{zcl}_G(f)$, is the largest non-negative integer $n$ for which there exists cohomology classes $\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_k\in H_G^{\ast}(Y\times Y)$ satisfying $\Delta_Y^*(\alpha_i)=0$ for each $i=0,\dots,n$ and $(f\times f)^*(\alpha_1\cup \alpha_2\cdots\cup \alpha)\neq 0$. Here $\Delta_Y\colon Y\to Y\times Y$ denotes the diagonal map. In other words,
    \[\mathbf{zcl}_G(f):= \mathrm{nil}\big(\mathrm{im}(\ker(\Delta_Y)_G^{h*}\xrightarrow{(f\times f)^*} \ker (\Delta_X)_G^{h*})\big).\]
<!-- end definition-14 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{properties_of_tc_of_maps}
Let $f, f_1, f_2\colon X\to Y$ and $g\colon Y\to Z$ be $G$-maps.
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $\mathbf{TC}_G(\mathrm{id}_X)=\mathbf{TC}_G(X)$.
        \item $\mathbf{TC}_G(f)\leq \mathrm{min}\big\{ \mathbf{TC}_G(X), \mathbf{TC}_G(Y)\big\}$.
        \item Let $H$ and $H'$ be closed subgroups of $G$ such that $X^H, Y^H$ are $H'$-invariant. Then $\mathbf{TC}_{H'}(f^H)\leq \mathbf{TC}_G(f)$.
        \item $\mathbf{cat}_H(f)\leq \mathbf{TC}_G(f)$, if $H$ is a stablizer of some point in $X$.
        \item $\mathbf{TC}_G(f)\leq \mathbf{cat}_G(f\times f)$, if $Y$ is $G$-connected.
        \item $\mathbf{TC}_G(g\circ f)\leq \mathrm{min}\big\{\mathbf{TC}_G(f),\mathbf{TC}_G(g)\big\}$.
        \item $\mathbf{TC}_G(f_1)=\mathbf{TC}_G(f_2)$, if $f_1$ is $G$-homotopic to $f_2$.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- definition-15: body_md -->
\label{LS_cat}
Let $X_\bullet\colon (\mathbb{R}_{\geq 0},\leq)\to \mathcal{C}^G$ be a persistent $G$-space.                                                                                      
The \emph{$G$-persistent Lusternik--Schnirelmann category} of $X_\bullet$ is the functor
\(\mathbf{cat}_G(X_\bullet)\colon
(\mathscr{Int},\subseteq)\longrightarrow
(\mathbb{N}\cup\{\infty\},\leq)\), defined by  \[\mathbf{cat}_G(X_{\bullet})([s,t])= \mathbf{cat}_G(f^s_t\colon X_s\to X_t), 
\]
where $\mathbf{cat}_G(f)$ denotes the equivariant LS category of the $G$-map $f$, introduced in \cite[Definition 4.2]{daundkar2025equivariant}.
<!-- end definition-15 -->
<!-- definition-16: body_md -->
Let $f:X\rightarrow Y$ be a $G$-map and $R$ be a commutative ring. Then the \emph{$G$-cup length} of $f$ id defined by ${\mathbf{cl}}_G(f;R):=\mathrm{nil}((f)_G^{h\ast}(\tilde H_G^\ast(Y))$.
<!-- end definition-16 -->
<!-- definition-17: body_md -->
\label{cup_length}
    Let $X_\bullet$ be a persistent $G$-space.
A \emph{$G$-persistent zero-divisor-cup-length} is the functor 
\(\mathbf{cl}_G(X_{\bullet};R)\colon (\mathscr{Int},\subseteq)\to (\mathbb{N}\cup \{\infty\}), \) defined by  \[\mathbf{cl}_G(X_{\bullet};R)([a,b])=\mathbf{cl}_G(f_a^b;R).\]
<!-- end definition-17 -->
<!-- definition-18: body_md -->
\label{G Categorical Invariant}
Let $\mathcal C^G$ be the category of $G$-objects in $\mathcal C$. A \emph{$G$-categorical invariant} is a map $\mathbf{I}^G: \operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C^G)\sqcup \operatorname{Mor}(\mathcal C^G) \longrightarrow (\mathbb R_{\geq 0},\leq)$ such that 
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $\mathbf{I}^G(\mathrm{id}_X)=\mathbf{I}^G(X)$ for every
    $X\in\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C^G)$;
    
    \item for any composable $G$-equivariant maps $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}Z\xrightarrow{h}W$
    in $\mathcal C^G$, one has
    \[
    \mathbf{I}^G(h\circ g\circ f)\leq \mathbf{I}^G(g).
    \]
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end definition-18 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lem: composition ineq}
    The $G$-cup length $\mathbf{cl}_G(-)$ satisfies
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item $\mathbf{cl}_G(\mathrm{id}_X)=\mathbf{cl}_G(X)$.
        \item If $f\colon X\to Y, g\colon Y\to Z$ and $h\colon Z\to W$ be $G$-maps, then $\mathbf{cl}_{G}(h\circ g\circ f)\leq \mathbf{cl}_G(g)$.
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
We note that $(\mathrm{id}_X)_G^{h*}(\tilde{H}_G^*(X;R))= \tilde{H}_G^*(X;R)$. Hence $\mathbf{cl}_G(\mathrm{id}_X;R)=\mathrm{nil}(\tilde{H}_G^*(X;R))=\mathbf{cl}_G(X)$.

    Suppose $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}Z\xrightarrow{h} W$ be $G$-equivariant maps and $\mathbf{cl}_G(g;R)=k$. Then $(h\circ g\circ f)_G^{h*}= f_G^{h*}\circ g_G^{h*}\circ h_G^{h*}$. Hence $(h\circ g\circ f)_G^{h*}(\tilde{H}_G^{h*}(W;R))$. Let $u_1,\ldots,u_{k+1} \in (h\circ g\circ f)_G^{h*} (\tilde H_G^*(W;R))$. Hence, for each $i$, there exists $a_i\in g_G^{h*}(\tilde H_G^*(Z;R))$ such that $u_i=f_G^{h*}(a_i)$ and so $u_1\cup\cdots\cup u_{k+1}= f_G^{h*}(a_1\cup\cdots\cup a_{k+1})$. Since $\mathbf{cl}_G(g;R)=k$, we have $a_1\cup\cdots\cup a_{k+1}=0$. Thus $u_1\cup\cdots\cup u_{k+1}=0$. This gives $\mathbf{cl}_G(h\circ g\circ f;R) \leq k.$
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{lem: composition ineq for cat}
 Let $f: X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ be $G$-maps between $G$-spaces. Then 
 $$\mathbf{cat}_G(g\circ f)\leq min\{\mathbf{cat}_G(f),\mathbf{cat}_G(g)\}.$$
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
It is easy to see that $\mathbf{cat}_G(\mathrm{id}_X)=\mathbf{cat}_G(X)$. Now we show that $\mathbf{cat}_G(g\circ f)\leq min\{\mathbf{cat}_G(f),\mathbf{cat}_G(g)\}$. The inequality $\mathbf{cat}_G(g\circ f)\leq \mathbf{cat}_G(f)$ is obvious. To prove $\mathbf{cat}_G(g\circ f)\leq \mathbf{cat}_G(g)$, consider a $G$-invariant open set $V\subseteq Y$ such that $g|_{V}\simeq_G h$, where $h$ is a $G$-map taking values in an orbit of some point. Let $U=f^{-1}(V)$. Then $(g\circ f)|_{U}=g|_{V}\circ f|_{U}\simeq_G h\circ f|_{U}$. Note that since $h$ takes values in some orbit, $h\circ f|_{U}$ also takes values in the same orbit. This proves the desired inequality.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{Categorical invariance}
   $\mathbf{cl}_G,\mathbf{cat}_G\colon\mathrm{Ob}(\mathrm{Top}^G)\sqcup \mathrm{Mor}(\mathrm{Top}^G)\rightarrow \mathbb N\cup\{\infty\}$ are $G$-categorical invariants.
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
Follows from Lemma \ref{lem: composition ineq} and Lemma \ref{lem: composition ineq for cat}.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
Let $(X,d)$ be a metric space equipped with an action of a group $G$ by isometries. For $r>0$, the Vietoris-Rips complex $\mathrm{VR}_{\leq r}(X)$ admits a natural simplicial $G$-action defined on simplices by
\[
g\cdot\{x_0,\ldots,x_k\} = \{g x_0,\ldots,g x_k\}, \text{ for all }g\in G.
\]
Moreover, $d(g\,x, g\,y)=g(x,y)$ for all $x,y\in X$ and $g\in G$. 
Thus $\mathrm{VR}_{\bullet}(X)$ is naturally a $G$-persistent space.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
Suppose $\mathbb{Z}_2$ acts on $\mathbb{S}^n$ by reflection in the last coordinate. Then 
    \[\mathbf{cat}_{\mathbb{Z}_2}(\mathrm{VR}_{\bullet}(\mathbb{S}^n))(J)=
    \begin{cases}
    1,& \text{if } J\subset  \big(0,\mathrm{arccos}(-\frac{1}{n+1})\big),\\
        0, & \text{if } J\not\subset [0,\pi].
    \end{cases}\]
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
By \cite[Theorem 8]{LM25}, $\mathrm{VR}_t(\mathbb{S}^n)\simeq_{\mathbb{Z}_2} \mathbb{S}^n$ for $0<t<\arccos\left(-\frac{1}{n+1}\right)$. Moreover, $\mathrm{cat}_{\mathbb{Z}_2}(S^n)=1$ (see \cite[Example 5.9]{Colman_Grant_Eqtc}). Then the result follows.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{Cat_cal_3}
    Let $\mathbb{Z}_2$ acts on $\mathbb{CP}^n$ by complex conjugation. Then $\mathbf{cat}_{\mathbb{Z}_2}(\mathbb{CP}^n)=n$.
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
We note that $(\mathbb{CP}^n)^{\mathbb{Z}_2}=\mathbb{RP}^n$. This implies that $\mathbf{cat}_{\mathbb{Z}_2}(\mathbb{CP}^n)\geq \mathbf{cat}(\mathbb{RP}^n)=n$.

    Next consider the open sets $U_j=\{[z_0,\dots,z_n]\in \mathbb{CP}^n\mid z_j\neq 0\}$ for $0\leq j\leq n$. Clearly, $\mathbb{CP}^n=\bigcup_{j=0}^n U_j$.

    Let $\phi\colon U_j\to \mathbb{C}^n$ be defined as
    \[\phi_j([z_0,\dots,z_n]):=\big(\frac{z_0}{z_j},\dots, \frac{z_{j-1}}{z_j},\frac{z_{j+1}}{z_j},\dots,\frac{z_n}{z_j}\big).\]

    One can show $\phi_j$ is a homeomorphism with inverse given by \[(w_1,\dots,w_n)\mapsto [w_1,\dots,w_{j-1},1,w_{j+1},\dots, w_n].\]
    Note that under this homeomorphism $p_j=[0,\dots,0,1,0\dots,0]$ is mapped to $(0,\dots,0)$.

    Now consider the homotopy $H_j\colon \mathbb{C}^n\times I\to \mathbb{C}^n$ defined by $$H(w_1,\dots,w_n,t)=\big((1-t)w_1,\dots,(1-t)w_n\big).$$ Note that $H(\bar{w}_1,\dots,\bar{w}_n,t)= \overline{H(w_1,\dots,w_n,t)}$. This gives that the inclusion $i_j\colon U_j\hookrightarrow \mathbb{CP}^n$ is $\mathbb{Z}_2$-homotopic to a map $c_j\colon U_j\to \mathbb{CP}^n$ given by $c_j(x)=p_j$. Also, the image of $c_j$ is contained in the single orbit of $\{p_j\}$. This gives that each $U_j$ is $\mathbb{Z}_2$-categorical. Hence $\mathbf{cat}_{\mathbb{Z}_2}(\mathbb{CP}^n)\leq n$. This completes the proof.
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
\Cref{Cat_cal_3} is a special case of \cite[Theorem 3.2]{BDS26}, where the result is proved for quasitoric manifolds from a different perspective. $\mathbb{C} P^n$ is an example of a quasitoric manifold. Here we have given a direct proof.
<!-- end remark-2 -->
<!-- definition-19: body_md -->
\label{per_tc}
Let $X_\bullet$ be a persistent $G$-space.
A \emph{$G$-persistent topological complexity} is the functor 
\(\mathbf{TC}_G(X_{\bullet})\colon (\mathscr{Int},\subseteq)\to (\mathbb{N}\cup \{0\})\),  defined by  \[\mathbf{TC}_G(X_{\bullet})([a,b])=\mathbf{TC}_G(f^b_a:X_a\to X_b).\]
<!-- end definition-19 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
Let $X_\bullet$ be a persistent $G$-space, and let $H,H'$ be closed
subgroups of $G$. If $X_a^H,Y_a^H$ are $H'$-invariant for every $a\in\mathbb{R}$,
then
\[
\mathbf{TC}_{H'}(X_\bullet^H)([a,b])
\leq
\mathbf{TC}_G(X_\bullet)([a,b])
\]
for every $[a,b]\in\mathscr{Int}$.
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- proposition-4: body_md -->
\label{TC_cal}
    Suppose $\mathbb Z_2$ acts on $\mathbb{S}^n$ by reflection with respect to the last coordinate. Then 
    \[\mathbf{TC}_{Z_2}(\mathrm{VR}_{\bullet}(\mathbb{S}^n))(J)=\begin{cases}
                                                                                      
                                                                                                              
     3, & \text{if } n\geq 2 \text{ and } J\subset \big(0,\mathrm{arccos}(-\frac{1}{n+1})\big),\\
        0, & \text{if } J\not\subset [0,\pi].
    \end{cases}\]
<!-- end proposition-4 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
By \cite[Theorem 8]{LM25}, $\mathrm{VR}_t(\mathbb{S}^n)\simeq_{\mathbb{Z}_2} \mathbb{S}^n$ for $0<t<\arccos\left(-\frac{1}{n+1}\right)$. 
On the other hand, for $t>\pi$, every pair of points in $\mathbb{S}^n$
has geodesic distance at most $\pi<t$. Hence $\mathrm{VR}_t(\mathbb{S}^n)$ is the abstract simplex on the vertex set $\mathbb{S}^n$, and therefore $\mathrm{VR}_t(\mathbb{S}^n)\simeq *$. Consequently, if $t\not \in [0,\pi]$, then
$\mathrm{VR}_t(\mathbb{S}^n)$ is contractible.
Combining these observations with
$\mathbf{TC}_{\mathbb{Z}_2}(\mathbb{S}^n)= 3$
for $n\geq 3$ from \cite[Example 5.9]{Colman_Grant_Eqtc}, gives the desired result.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- definition-20: body_md -->
\label{zcl}
    Let $X_\bullet$ be a persistent $G$-space.
A \emph{$G$-persistent zero-divisor-cup-length} is the functor 
\(\mathbf{zcl}_G(X_{\bullet};R)\colon (\mathscr{Int},\subseteq)\to (\mathbb{N}\cup \{\infty\}), \) defined by  \[\mathbf{zcl}_G(X_{\bullet};R)([a,b])=\mathbf{zcl}_G(f_a^b;R).\]
<!-- end definition-20 -->
<!-- proposition-5: body_md -->
\label{Categorical invariance 2}
   $\mathbf{zcl}_G,\mathbf{TC}_G\colon \mathrm{Ob}(\mathrm{Top}^G)\sqcup \mathrm{Mor}(\mathrm{Top}^G)\rightarrow \mathbb N\cup\{\infty\}$ are $G$-categorical invariants.
<!-- end proposition-5 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
For $\mathbf{I}^G= \mathbf{zcl}_G, \mathbf{TC}_G$, we know that $\mathbf{I}^G(\mathrm{id}_X)=\mathbf{I}^G(X)$ for all $G$-spaces $X$.
    Moreover, $\mathbf{I}^G(f\circ g)\leq \min\{\mathbf{I}^G(f),\mathbf{I}^G(g)\}$ for all $G$-maps $X\xrightarrow{g}Y\xrightarrow{f}Z$ (see \cite{daundkar2026equivariant}).
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- proposition-6: body_md -->
Let $X_{\bullet}$ be a persistent $G$-space. Then
$$\mathbf{cl}_G(X_{\bullet})\leq \mathbf{cat}_G(X_{\bullet})\leq \mathbf{TC}_G(X_{\bullet}).$$
<!-- end proposition-6 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
The proof follows from the following inequalities
    $$\mathbf{cl}_G(X_\bullet)[a,b]=\mathbf{cl}_G(f_a^b)\leq \mathbf{cat}_G(f_a^b)\leq \mathbf{TC}_G(f_a^b).$$
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
\label{lowerbound}
Let $f\colon X\to Y$ be a $G$-map. Suppose $u_i\in H_G^*(X\times X;R)$ satisfy $u_i\in
\ker((\Delta_X)_G^{h*})\cap \mathrm{im}\bigl((f\times f)_G^{h*}\bigr)$ for $0\leq i\leq k$, where $R$ is a commutative ring. If $u_0\cup \dots\cup u_k\neq 0$, then $k+1\leq \mathbf{TC}_G(f)$.
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- proposition-7: body_md -->
Let $X_{\bullet}$ be a persistent $G$-space. Then 
    \[\mathbf{zcl}_G(X_{\bullet};R)\leq \mathbf{TC}_G(X_{\bullet}).\]
<!-- end proposition-7 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
\label{zcl_cal}
    Let $\mathbb{Z}_2$ act on $\mathbb{S}^n$ by reflection in the last coordinate. Then 
    \[\mathbf{zcl}_{\mathbb{Z}_2}(\mathbb{S}^n;\mathbb{Q})=1.\]
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
Suppose the action of $\mathbb{Z}_2$ on $\mathbb{S}^n$ is given by the map $\alpha\colon \mathbb{S}^n\to S^n$, defined as $$\alpha(x_1,\dots,x_n)=(x_1,\dots,x_{n-1},-x_n).$$ Then if $u$ be the generator of $H^n(\mathbb{S}^n;\mathbb{Q})$, then $\alpha^*(u)=-u$. This implies that $H_{\mathbb{Z}_2}^*(\mathbb{S}^n;\mathbb{Q})=H^*(\mathbb{S}^n;\mathbb{Q})^{\mathbb{Z}_2}=\mathbb{Q}$.

Now we analyze $H_{\mathbb{Z}_2}(\mathbb{S}^n\times \mathbb{S}^n;\mathbb{Q})= H^*(\mathbb{S}^n\times \mathbb{S}^n;\mathbb{Q})^{\mathbb{Z}_2}$. Using Kunneth formula, we note that $u_1=1\otimes u$ and $u_2=u\otimes 1$ are the generators of $H^n(\mathbb{S}^n\times \mathbb{S}^n;\mathbb{Q})$ and $u_1 \cup u_2= u\otimes u$ is the generator of $H^{2n}(\mathbb{S}^n\times \mathbb{S}^n;\mathbb{Q})$. Clearly $\alpha^*(u_1)=-u_1$ and $\alpha^*(u_2)=-u_2$. Therefore $\alpha^*(u_1\cup u_2)= u_1 \cup u_2$. Thus $H^*(\mathbb{S}^n\times \mathbb{S}^n;\mathbb{Q})^{\mathbb{Z}_2}\cong \mathbb{Q}\oplus \mathbb{Q}\{u_1\cup u_2\}$. 

It follows from $\Delta_{\mathbb{S}^n}^*(u_1)=u= \Delta_{\mathbb{S}^n}^*(u_2)$ that the homomorphism  $$(\Delta_{\mathbb{S}^n})_{\mathbb{Z}_2}^{h\ast}\colon H_{\mathbb{Z}_2}^*(\mathbb{S}^n\times \mathbb{S}^n;\mathbb{Q})\to H_{\mathbb{Z}_2}^*(\mathbb{S}^n;\mathbb{Q})$$ satisfies $(\Delta_{\mathbb{S}^n})_{\mathbb{Z}_2}^{h\ast}(u_1\cup u_2)= u^2=0$. Hence $u_1\cup u_2\in \ker((\Delta_{\mathbb{S}^n})_{\mathbb{Z}_2}^{h\ast})$ is the only non-zero class, so $\mathbf{zcl}_{\mathbb{Z}_2}(\mathbb{S}^n)= 1$.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- lemma-7: body_md -->
Suppose $\mathbb{S}^1$ acts on $X=\mathbb{S}^1$ by rotation. Then
    \[\mathbf{zcl}_{\mathbb{S}^1}(\mathbb{S}^1;\mathbb{Q})=1.\]
<!-- end lemma-7 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
Here the action is free and transitive, so $H_{\mathbb{S}^1}^*(X;\mathbb{Q})\cong H^*(X/{\mathbb{S}^1};\mathbb{Q})\cong \mathbb{Q}$. 
 Also $H_{\mathbb{S}^1}^*(X\times X;\mathbb{Q})\cong H^*(X\times X/{\mathbb{S}^1};\mathbb{Q})\cong H^*(\mathbb{S}^1;\mathbb{Q})\cong \mathbb{Q}\oplus \mathbb{Q}\{u\}$, where $u$ is the generator of $H_{\mathbb{S}^1}^1(X\times X;\mathbb{Q})$. This gives that $(\Delta_X)_{\mathbb{S}^1}^{h\ast}$ is trivial. Hence $u\in \ker((\Delta_X)_{\mathbb{S}^1}^{h\ast})$. As $u^2=0$, we have $\mathbf{zcl}_{\mathbb{S}^1}(\mathbb{S}^1;\mathbb{Q})=1$.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- lemma-8: body_md -->
Let $\mathbb{Z}_2$ acts on $\mathbb{CP}^n$ by complex conjugation. Then $\mathbf{zcl}_{\mathbb{Z}_2}(\mathbb{CP}^n;\mathbb{Q})\geq n$.
<!-- end lemma-8 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
Let $\tau\colon \mathbb{CP}^n\to \mathbb{CP}^n$ given by $\tau([z_1,\dots,z_n])=[\bar{z}_1,\dots,\bar{z}_n]$ represents the $\mathbb{Z}_2$-action on $\mathbb{CP}^n$.

    If $u$ be the generator of $H^2(\mathbb{CP}^n;\mathbb{Q})$, then we have $\tau^*(u^k)=(-1)^k u^k$. This implies that 
    \[H_{\mathbb{Z}_2}^*(\mathbb{CP}^n;\mathbb{Q})\cong H^*(\mathbb{CP}^n;\mathbb{Q})^{\mathbb{Z}_2}\cong 
    \begin{cases}
      \mathbb{Q}\oplus \mathbb{Q}\{u^2\}\oplus \dots\oplus\mathbb{Q}\{u^{2n}\}, \text{ if } n \text{ is even},\\
       \mathbb{Q}\oplus \mathbb{Q}\{u^2\}\oplus \dots\oplus\mathbb{Q}\{u^{2n-2}\}, \text{ if } n \text{ is odd}.
    \end{cases}
    \]
    Similarly, we have \[H_{\mathbb{Z}_2}^*(\mathbb{CP}^n\times \mathbb{CP}^n;\mathbb{Q})\cong \big(\frac{\mathbb{Q}[u,v]}{u^{n+1}, v^{n+1}}\big)^{\mathbb{Z}_2}.\]
    Note that $u^kv^l\in H_{\mathbb{Z}_2}^*(\mathbb{CP}^n\times \mathbb{CP}^n;\mathbb{Q})$ if either $k$ and $l$ are both odd or $k$ and $l$ are both even. Also $u^{2i}, v^{2i}\in H_{\mathbb{Z}_2}^*(\mathbb{CP}^n\times \mathbb{CP}^n;\mathbb{Q})$ for $i=1,\dots,\lfloor \frac{n}{2} \rfloor+1$.

    Since $\Delta_X^*\colon H^*(\mathbb{CP}^n\times \mathbb{CP}^n;\mathbb{Q})\to H^*(\mathbb{CP}^n;\mathbb{Q})$ maps both $u$ and $v$ to $u$, we have $uv-u^2\in \ker(\Delta_X)_{\mathbb{Z}_2}^{h*}$. As $(uv-u^2)^n\neq 0$ in $H_{\mathbb{Z}_2}^*(\mathbb{CP}^n\times \mathbb{CP}^n;\mathbb{Q})$, $\mathbf{zcl}_{\mathbb{Z}_2}(\mathbb{CP}^n;\mathbb{Q})\geq n$.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- proposition-8: body_md -->
Suppose $\mathbb{Z}_2$ acts on $\mathbb{S}^n$ by reflection in the last coordinate. Then 
    \[\mathbf{zcl}_{\mathbb{Z}_2}(\mathrm{VR}_{\bullet}(\mathbb{S}^n))(J)=
    \begin{cases}
    1,& \text{if } J\subset  \big(0,\mathrm{arccos}(-\frac{1}{n+1})\big),\\
        0, & \text{if } J\not\subset [0,\pi].
    \end{cases}\]
<!-- end proposition-8 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
Using a similar argument as in Proposition~\ref{TC_cal}, we obtain the result from Lemma~\ref{zcl_cal}.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- definition-21: body_md -->
The \emph{$G$-homotopy interleaving distance} $d_{HI}^G$ between persistent $G$-spaces $X_{\bullet}$ and $Y_{\bullet}$ is defined as follows:
    \[d_{HI}^G(X_{\bullet},Y_{\bullet}):=\mathrm{inf}\{d_{I}^{Top^G}(X_{\bullet}',Y_{\bullet}')\mid X_{\bullet}'\simeq^G X_{\bullet}, Y_{\bullet}'\simeq^G Y_{\bullet}\}.\]
<!-- end definition-21 -->
<!-- definition-22: body_md -->
Given a $G$-space $T$ and a $G$-equivariant function (not necessarily continuous) $\gamma:T\to \mathbb R$, we can define the \emph{sublevel filtration} $\mathcal S(\gamma):\mathbb R\to \mathrm{Top}^G$ by 
    $$\mathcal S(\gamma)_r=\gamma^{-1}(-\infty,r].$$
     Clearly, $\mathcal S(\gamma)_r$ is a $G$-invariant subset of $T$, since $\gamma$ is a $G$-function.
<!-- end definition-22 -->
<!-- definition-23: body_md -->
A  $G$-invariant distance $d^G$ on $G$-spaces is
    \begin{enumerate}
        \item \emph{stable} if for all $G$-spaces $X$ and $G$-functions $\gamma,\gamma':X\to \mathbb{R}$,
        $$d^G(\mathcal S(\gamma), \mathcal S(\gamma'))\leq d_{\infty}(\gamma,\gamma'),$$
        \item \emph{homotopy invariant} if $d^G(X,Y)=0$ for all $X\simeq^G Y.$
    \end{enumerate}
<!-- end definition-23 -->
<!-- remark-3: body_md -->
Let $\mathbf{I}$ be a categorical invariant. Then, we have the following inequality for any $G$-persistent object $X_\bullet, Y_{\bullet}\colon (\mathbb R,\leq)\rightarrow \mathcal C^G$
    \[d_{E}(\mathbf{I}(X_{\bullet}),\mathbf{I}(Y_{\bullet}))\leq d_{E}^G(\mathbf{I}(X_{\bullet}),\mathbf{I}(Y_{\bullet}))\leq d_{I}^G(X_{\bullet},Y_{\bullet}),\] where $d_E$ denotes the errosion distance.
<!-- end remark-3 -->
<!-- remark-4: body_md -->
Let $\mathbf{I}$ be a categorical invariant of topological spaces such that it is invariant under pre- and post-composition with weak homotopy equivalences. Then for any persistent $G$-spaces $X_{\bullet}$ and $Y_{\bullet}$, we have 
    \[d_E(\mathbf{I}(X_{\bullet}), \mathbf{I}(Y_{\bullet}))\leq d_{HI}^G(X_{\bullet}, Y_{\bullet})\] and
                                                        
    \[d_E(\mathbf{I}(\mathrm{VR}_{\bullet}(X), \mathbf{I}(\mathrm{VR}_{\bullet}(Y)))\leq 2 \cdot d_{GH}^G(X,Y).\]
<!-- end remark-4 -->
<!-- definition-24: body_md -->
\label{errosion}
Let $X_{\bullet}, Y_{\bullet}$ be $G$-persistent spaces. Let
$\mathbf{I}_X^G,\mathbf{I}_Y^G: (\mathscr{Int},\subseteq)\to (\mathbb{R}_{\geq0},\leq)$
be interval invariants associated to $X_{\bullet}$ and
$Y_{\bullet}$, respectively. For $\epsilon>0$, we call $\mathbf{I}_X^G$ and $\mathbf{I}_Y^G$ are \emph{$\epsilon$-erroded} if for every $[a,b]\in \mathscr{Int}$, 
\[\mathbf{I}_X^G([a,b])\geq \mathbf{I}_Y^G([a-\epsilon, b+\epsilon])\text{ and } \mathbf{I}_Y^G([a,b])\geq \mathbf{I}_X^G([a-\epsilon,b+\epsilon]).\]

The $G$-equivariant erosion distance between $X_{\bullet}$ and $Y_{\bullet}$ is defined by
\[d_E^G(X_{\bullet}, Y_{\bullet}):= \mathrm{inf}\big\{\epsilon>0\mid \mathbf{I}_X^G\text{ and }\mathbf{I}_Y^G \text{ are $\varepsilon$-eroded} \big\}.,\]
 with the convension that $d_E^G(X_{\bullet}, Y_{\bullet})=\infty$ if no such $\epsilon$ exists.
<!-- end definition-24 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{E vs GI}
    Let $\mathbf{I}^G\colon \operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C^G)\sqcup \operatorname{Mor}(\mathcal C^G) \longrightarrow (\mathbb R_{\geq 0},\leq)$ be $G$-equivariant categorical invariant of $\mathcal{C}^G$. Then for any persistent $G$-spaces $X_{\bullet}$ and $Y_{\bullet}$ in $\mathcal{C}$, we have 
    \[d_E^G(\mathbf{I}^G(X_{\bullet}), \mathbf{I}^G(Y_{\bullet}))\leq d_{I}^G(X_{\bullet}, Y_{\bullet}).\]
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
The proof is identical to that of \cite[Theorem 1]{MSZ24}, with the ordinary categorical invariant and morphisms replaced by their $G$-equivariant counterparts in $\mathcal C^G$.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- lemma-9: body_md -->
\label{I^G_property}
    Let $\mathbf{I}^G$ be a $G$-categorical invariant such that for any $G$-equivariant maps $X\xrightarrow{f} Y\xrightarrow{g} Z\xrightarrow{h}W$ in $\mathcal{C}^G$, if $g$ is a $G$-weak homotopy equivalence, then $\mathbf{I}^G(g\circ f)= \mathbf{I}^G(f)$ and $\mathbf{I}^G(h\circ g)=\mathbf{I}^G(h)$. If the $G$-persistent spaces $X_{\bullet}$ and $X_{\bullet}'$ are such that $X_{\bullet}\simeq^G X_{\bullet}'$, then $\mathbf{I}^G(X_{\bullet})=\mathbf{I}^G(X_{\bullet}')$.
<!-- end lemma-9 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
Since $X_{\bullet}\simeq^G X'{\bullet}$, there exists a $G$-persistent space $W_{\bullet}$ and objectwise $G$-weak equivalences $\phi\colon W_{\bullet}\Rightarrow X_{\bullet}$ and $\psi\colon W_{\bullet}\Rightarrow X_{\bullet}'$. This implies that for each $t\in \mathbb{R}$, the maps $\phi_t\colon W_t\to X_t$ and $\psi_t\colon W_t\to X_t'$ are $G$-weak homotopy equivalence. Using this, it follows from the following commutative diagram
\[\begin{tikzcd}
	{Z_t} & {Z_s} \\
	{X_t} & {X_s}
	\arrow["{g_t^s}", from=1-1, to=1-2]
	\arrow["{\phi_t}"', "\simeq",from=1-1, to=2-1]
	\arrow["{\phi_s}"', "\simeq",from=1-2, to=2-2]
	\arrow["{f_t^s}"', from=2-1, to=2-2]
\end{tikzcd}\]
    that   \[\begin{aligned}
\mathbf{I}_X^G([t,s])
&=\mathbf{I}^G(f_s^t) =\mathbf{I}^G(f_s^t\circ \phi_t) =\mathbf{I}^G(\phi_s\circ g_s^t) =\mathbf{I}^G(g_s^t) =\mathbf{I}_W^G([t,s]).
\end{aligned}\]
Hence $\mathbf{I}^G(X_{\bullet})= \mathbf{I}^G(W_{\bullet})$. Similarly, we can show that $I(X_{\bullet}')= \mathbf{I}^G(W_{\bullet})$. Consequently, $\mathbf{I}^G(X_{\bullet})= \mathbf{I}^G(X_{\bullet}')$.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- proposition-9: body_md -->
\label{prop: d^G VR leq 2d_GH}
    A stable and $G$-homootopy invariant distance $d^G$ on $G$-equivariant metric spaces satisfies $$d^G(\mathrm{VR}_{\bullet}({X}),\mathrm{VR}_{\bullet}({Y}))\leq2\cdot d_{GH}^G(X,Y).$$
<!-- end proposition-9 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
Let $X, Y$ be two metric $G$-spaces with ${d}_{GH}^{G}({X},{Y})<\delta.$
    Then there exists $G$-invariant subset $C\subseteq X\times Y$ with $|d_X^G(x,x')-d_Y^G(y,y')|\leq2\delta,$ for all $(x,y), (x',y')\in C.$
    Let $[C]$ be the full simplicial complex formed by the vertex set $C.$ We note that $[C]$ is a $G$-space. We also have the $G$-equivariant projection maps $p_X\colon C\to X$ and $p_Y\colon C\to Y.$

    We define a filtration $F_\bullet^X$ on $[C]$ where $\sigma\in F^X_r$ if and only if ${d}_{X}^{G}({p_X(u)},{p_X(v)})\leq 2r$ for all $u,v \in \sigma.$
    We note that for all $gu,gv \in g\sigma$,
    \begin{align*}
        d_X^G(p_X(gu),p_X(gv))&= d_X^G(gp_X(u),gp_X(v)) & \text{ (since the projection } p_X \text{ is } G\text{-equivariant)}\\
        &= d_X^G(p_X(u),p_X(v)) & \text{ (since the metric } d_X^G \text{ is } G\text{-equivariant)}\\
        &\leq 2r.
    \end{align*}
    Thus $F_\bullet^X$ is a $G$-simplicial filtration.
    This induces a $G$-function $\gamma^X\colon [C]\to \mathbb{R}$ given by $$\gamma^X(\sigma)=\min\{r\in \mathbb{R}\mid \sigma\in F_r^X\}.$$ Therefore $F_\bullet^X=\mathcal S(\gamma^X)$ is the $G$-simplicial sublevel filtration.
    Similarly, we define a filtration $F_\bullet^Y$ so that $F_\bullet^Y=\mathcal S(\gamma^Y).$

     We have ${d}_{\infty}^{}({\gamma^X},{\gamma^Y})=\sup_{\sigma\in [C]} |\gamma^X(\sigma)-\gamma^Y(\sigma)|\leq \delta.$
     By stability assumption for $d^G$, we obtain
     $$d^G(F_\bullet^X,F_\bullet^Y)=d^G(\mathcal S(\gamma^X),\mathcal S(\gamma^Y))\leq d_\infty(\gamma^X,\gamma^Y)\leq \delta.$$
     We note that $p_X:C\to X$ induces a $G$-equivariant simplicial map $g_r:F^X_{r/2}\to \mathrm{VR}_r(X)$. 
     The equivariant Quillen's Theorem A \cite[Theorem A.2]{Bergner_eqTree} says that if $f:S\to T$ is a $G$-simplicial map of $G$-simplicial complexes such that $(f^H)^{-1}(\sigma)$ is contractible for all subgroups $H\leq G$, then $f$ is a $G$-homotopy equivalence. By Quillen's Theorem A,  we conclude $g_r$ is a $G$-homotopy equivalence for all $r\geq 0.$ Thus $g: F_{\bullet/2}^X\to \mathrm{VR}_{\bullet}({X})$ is an objectwise $G$-homotopy equivalence.
     Similarly, by considering the map $F^Y_{r}\to \mathrm{VR}_r(Y)$ induced from $p_Y:C\to Y$, we obtain a $G$-homotopy equivalence  $F_{\bullet/2}^Y\to \mathrm{VR}_{\bullet}({Y})$.
     Using the $G$-homootopy invariance assumption for $d^G$, we have $d^G(\mathrm{VR}_{\bullet}({X}) ,F_{\bullet/2}^X)=0$ and $d^G(\mathrm{VR}_{\bullet}({Y}),F_{\bullet/2}^Y)=0.$

     Using the triangle inequality, this yields
     $$d^G(\mathrm{VR}_{\bullet}({X}), \mathrm{VR}_{\bullet}({Y}))\leq d^G(\mathrm{VR}_{\bullet}({X}) ,F_{\bullet/2}^X)+ d^G(F_{\bullet/2}^X,F_{\bullet/2}^Y) +d^G(\mathrm{VR}_{\bullet}({Y}),F_{\bullet/2}^Y)\leq2\delta.$$
     Since the inequality holds for every $\delta>d_{GH}^G(X,Y)$, passing through the infimum, we get $d^G(\mathrm{VR}_{\bullet}({X}), \mathrm{VR}_{\bullet}({Y}))\leq 2d_{GH}^G(X,Y).$
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm: stability invariance}
$d_{HI}^G$ is a distance on $G$-spaces satisfies: \begin{enumerate}
    \item stability,
    \item $G$-homotopy invariance.
\end{enumerate}
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
It is clear from the definition of $d_{HI}^G$ is non-negative, symmetric and $d_{HI}^G(X,X)=0$ for any $G$-space $X$. The triangle inequality follows from similar arguments in \cite[section 4.2]{BL}.

    (1) Let $\gamma, \gamma'\colon X\to \mathbb{R}$ be two $G$-maps with $d_\infty(\gamma,\gamma')\leq \epsilon.$
    We have the inclusion of sublevel sets
    $$\mathcal{S}(\gamma)_r=\{x\in X|\gamma(t)\leq r\}\subseteq\{x\in X|\gamma'(t)\leq r+\epsilon\}=\mathcal{S}(\gamma')_{r+\epsilon}.$$
    We denote this inclusions by $\phi_r\colon \mathcal{S}(\gamma)_r\to \mathcal{S}(\gamma')_{r+\epsilon}.$
Symmetrically, we get inclusions $\psi_r:\mathcal{S}(\gamma')_r\to \mathcal{S}(\gamma)_{r+\epsilon}.$
The compositions $$\psi_{r+\epsilon}\circ\phi_r=\mathcal{S}(\gamma)(r \leq r+2\epsilon)$$ and $$\phi_{r+\epsilon}\circ\psi_r=\mathcal{S}(\gamma')(r \leq r+2\epsilon).$$ Consequently, $d_I^G(\mathcal{S}(\gamma),\mathcal{S}(\gamma'))\leq \epsilon.$
Therefore $d_{HI}^G(\mathcal{S}(\gamma),\mathcal{S}(\gamma'))\leq d_I^G(\mathcal{S}(\gamma),\mathcal{S}(\gamma'))\leq \epsilon.$
Thus $d_{HI}^G(\mathcal S(\gamma), \mathcal S(\gamma'))\leq d_\infty(\gamma, \gamma').
$

(2) For two $G$-spaces $X, Y$ with $X\simeq_G Y$, we have $d_{HI}^G(X,Y)\leq d_I(X,X)=0$ by the definition of homotopy interleaving distance.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{thm: HI between VR leq 2d_GH}
For $G$-metric spaces $X$ and $Y$, 
     $$d_{HI}^G(\mathrm{VR}_{\bullet}({X}),\mathrm{VR}_{\bullet}({Y}))\leq2\cdot d_{GH}^G(X,Y).$$
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{erosion_vs_homotopy_interleaving}
 Let $\mathbf{I}^G$ be a $G$-categorical invariant of topological spaces such that $\mathbf{I}^G$ is invariant under pre- and post-composition with $G$-weak homotopy equivalences. Then for persistent $G$-spaces $X_{\bullet}$ and $Y_{\bullet}$, we have 
    \begin{equation}            
        d_E^G(\mathbf{I}^G(X_{\bullet}), \mathbf{I}^G(Y_{\bullet}))\leq d_{HI}^G(X_{\bullet}, Y_{\bullet}).
    \end{equation}
    
    
    
    For compact $G$-metric spaces $(X,d_X)$ and $(Y,d_Y)$, we have 
    \begin{equation}\label{eq2}
        d_E^G(\mathbf{I}^G(\mathrm{VR}_{\bullet}(X)), \mathbf{I}^G(\mathrm{VR}_{\bullet}(Y)))\leq 2\cdot d_{GH}^G(X,Y).
    \end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
Let $X_{\bullet}', Y_{\bullet}'$ be two persistent $G$-spaces such that $X_{\bullet}\simeq^G X_{\bullet}'$ and $Y_{\bullet}\simeq^{G} Y_{\bullet}'$. Then by Lemma~\ref{I^G_property}, we have $d_E^G(\mathbf{I}^{G}(X_{\bullet}),\mathbf{I}^{G}(Y_{\bullet}))=d_E^G(\mathbf{I}^{G}(X_{\bullet}'),\mathbf{I}^{G}(Y_{\bullet}'))$. Hence it follows from Theorem~\ref{E vs GI} that $d_E^G(\mathbf{I}^{G}(X_{\bullet}), \mathbf{I}^{G}(Y_{\bullet}))\leq d_{I}^G(X_{\bullet}',Y_{\bullet}')$. Therefore, by the definition of the homotopy $G$-interleaving distance $d_E^G(\mathbf{I}^G(X_{\bullet}), \mathbf{I}^G(Y_{\bullet}))\leq d_{HI}^G(X_{\bullet}, Y_{\bullet})$.

    Combining this inequality with Corollary~\ref{thm: HI between VR leq 2d_GH}, we obtain \[d_E^G(\mathbf{I}^G(\mathrm{VR}_{\bullet}(X)), \mathbf{I}^G(\mathrm{VR}_{\bullet}(Y)))\leq 2\cdot d_{GH}^G(X,Y).\]
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
\label{corollary: erosion bounds}
Let $\mathbf{I}^G=\mathbf{cl}_G$, $\mathbf{zcl}_G, \mathbf{cat}_G$ or $\mathbf{TC}_G$.
    Suppose $X_{\bullet}$ and $Y_{\bullet}$ be two persistence $G$-spaces with $G$-CW complex structures. Then 
    \[d_{E}^G(\mathbf{I}^G(X_{\bullet}),\mathbf{I}^G(Y_{\bullet}))\leq d_{HI}^G(X_{\bullet},Y_{\bullet}).\]

    Moreover, for compact $G$-metric spaces $X$ and $Y$, we have 
    \[d_E^G(\mathbf{I}^G(\mathrm{VR}_{\bullet}(X)),\mathbf{I}^G(\mathrm{VR}_{\bullet}(Y)))\leq 2\cdot d_{GH}^G(X,Y).\]
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
Recall the equivariant Whitehead's theorem (see \cite{Bredon1967EquivariantCohomology}) if $f\colon X\to Y$ is a $G$-weak homotopy equivalence between $G$-spaces admitting a $G$-CW structure, then $f$ is a $G$-homotopy equivalence. Moreover, $\mathbf{cl}_G, \mathbf{cat}_G, \mathbf{zcl}_G$ and $\mathbf{TC}_G$ are invariant under post and pre-composition with $G$-homotopy equivalence by Propositions~\ref{Categorical invariance} and \ref{Categorical invariance 2}. Now the desired inequality follows from Theorem~\ref{erosion_vs_homotopy_interleaving}.

    Since Vietoris–Rips filtrations of compact metric spaces with $G$-action are persistent $G$-CW complexes, the second inequality is a consequence of~\eqref{eq2}.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- proposition-10: body_md -->
\label{lower_bound}
    Let $b>0$ and let $a_x,a_y$ be positive real numbers such that $\tfrac{b}{2}< a_y< a_x< b$. Suppose $X_{\bullet}$ and $Y_{\bullet}$ be $G$-persistence spaces with associated $G$-categorical invariants satisfy
    \[\mathbf{I}_X^G(J)=\begin{cases}
        n& \text{if } J\subset (0,a_x),\\
        0& \text{if } J\not\subset [0,b],
    \end{cases}
    \quad \mathbf{I}_Y^G(J)=\begin{cases}
        m & \text{if } J\subset (0,a_y),\\
        0&\text{if } J\not\subset [0,b],
    \end{cases}\]
    where $n> m>0$.
    Then $d_E^G(X_{\bullet}, Y_{\bullet})\geq \tfrac{a_x}{2}$.

    Moreover, if $\mathbf{I}_X^G(J)=0$ whenever the length of $J$ exceeds $a_x$ and $\mathbf{I}_Y^G(J)=0$ whenever the length of $J$ is grater than $a_y$, then $d_E^G(X_{\bullet}, Y_{\bullet})= \tfrac{a_x}{2}$.
<!-- end proposition-10 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
The proof is identical to that of \cite[Proposition 4.6]{mavsmoli2025persistence}, with $\mathbf{I}_X$ and $\mathbf{I}_Y$ replaced by $\mathbf{I}_X^G$ and $\mathbf{I}_Y^G$, respectively.
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- corollary-3: body_md -->
Let $n\geq 1$. Suppose $\mathbb{Z}_2$ acts on $\mathbb{S}^n$ by reflection in the last coordinate. Then
\[d_E^{\mathbb{Z}_2}(\mathbf{TC}_{\mathbb{Z}_2}(\mathrm{VR}_{\bullet}(\mathbb{S}^1), \mathbf{TC}_{\mathbb{Z}_2}(\mathrm{VR}_{\bullet}(\mathbb{S}^2))))\geq \frac{\alpha_1}{2}.\]
<!-- end corollary-3 -->
